catalog_quote: The basic tendency is to stress the last syllable; however, there are quite a few polysyllables which are not stressed on their last syllables. These are either exceptions in which case they will be marked by an accute accent, or they are words with an unaccented suffix or postpostion; e. g. : kalám (5); amík (90, small), but amíkta or : amík-ta (90); alót (39), but alótip or : alót-ip ... Other such suffixes are : -ik, -up, -ap, -yak, -ti, -to, -te, -we, -ne, -age, -vo, -ga, -ho, -a, -ya, -way, -ey, -bara, -hon, -laten. The verbal suffixes of the Papuan tongues, however, take the stress; e. g. : goal-án (1063); fil-én (ib.); ahól va-ím (1064); fi-í (ib.). All genuine polysyllables are stressed on their last syllables; e. g. : ezemán (113); muditín (32); teherán (97); sikelekamán (40). Polysyllables formed by reduplication or compounding admit a secondary stress on the accented syllable…

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (68 pp., text layer present; extracted text). PDF p. 24 carries the running head 'Aloys Kasprus, S.V.D., [37-40, 1942-45]' and page number 734, section 'IV. Notes on the Sound Attributes. 1. Stress.' The quoted sentences are there verbatim, including the original spellings 'accute accent' and 'postpostion': 'The basic tendency is to stress the last syllable; however, there are quite a few polysyllables which are not stressed on their last syllables. These are either exceptions in which case they will be marked by an accute accent, or they are words with an unaccented suffix or postpostion.. The verbal suffixes of the Papuan tongues, however, take the stress.. All genuine polysyllable…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word; unaccented suffixes and postpositions stay outside the stressed domain (so the root-final syllable keeps the stress), while verbal suffixes take it. Exceptions exist and are marked with an acute in the wordlist. The statement is made jointly for all Mugil District languages in the paper (two Austronesian, Saker/Bargam, and the Garus dialects); only Ate (= Murupi) is singled out as deviating with penultimate stress in certain polysyllables, so Em (= Garus proper) follows the final-stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Reduplicated or compounded polysyllables carry a secondary stress on the accented syllable of each component, with main stress on the ultimate (or penultimate for Ate); reduplicated monosyllables each keep their own stress (p. 734).
new_statements.exceptions: 'Quite a few' polysyllables not stressed on the last syllable (marked with acute); words with an unaccented suffix/postposition (-ik, -up, -ap, -yak, -ti, -to, -te, -we, -ne, -age, -vo, -ga, -ho, -a, -ya, -way, -ey, -bara, -hon, -laten); Ate dialect (= Murupi mqw) stresses certain polysyllables (metathesised forms, some verb forms) on the penult; interrogative particles and sentence-final question suffixes -e/-u reduce other word stresses to a 'slur'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, from wordlist/citation forms recorded ca. 1930 by a missionary (pre-phonemic, Anthropos transcription); pooled statement for the district's languages rather than a Garus-only analysis; also remarks on phrase/sentence-level reduction under interrogatives.
new_statements.identity_note: Kasprus 1942/45 treats the 'Garus dialects' Em, Ate and A'e together. Glottolog/hh.bib identify Em = Garus [gyb, garu1246], Ate = Murupi [mqw], A'e (Rempini) = Rempi [rmp]; Z'graggen 1975 (B-41) likewise codes Em under Garus C18 and Ate under Murupi C14. Kasprus's final-stress rule is stated for all languages of the paper with Ate (Murupi) explicitly excepted as penult-stressing, so the rule is taken to describe Em = Garus proper. The statement is pooled across languages and pre-phonemic (fieldnotes ca. 1930), hence low confidence.

sources.note: Sec. IV.1 'Stress' (p. 734) and sec. V rule A (p. 736): words of all the Mugil District languages treated (Megiar, Matukar, Saker=Bargam, and the Garus dialects Em/Ate/A'e) are 'basically stressed on the last syllable'; exceptions marked with an acute; unaccented suffixes/postpositions do not take stress; verbal suffixes do; secondary stress on components of reduplications/compounds; only the Ate speech (= Murupi mqw) stresses certain polysyllable classes on the penult. Em = Garus [gyb] per Glottolog/Z'graggen.
